b1-v-entscheiden: You stand in front of two jackets in a shop for ten minutes. At last you choose the blue one and walk to the cash desk.
Two companies offer you a job. After thinking all week, you tell both of them which one you pick.
You and your friends cannot agree where to eat tonight. Someone must make the final choice. Which verb means 'to decide'?
b1-n-katastrophe: A huge flood destroys a whole town, and thousands of people lose their homes. What kind of event is this?
You forgot your passport, missed your flight and lost your hotel booking, all on the same day. You say it was a total ... day. Which noun fits?
On the news you see pictures of a terrible earthquake. Which word means 'disaster'?
b1-n-stoff: You go to a shop to buy cotton or wool by the metre, because you want to sew a dress yourself.
A tailor shows you rolls in different colours and patterns for your new suit and lets you touch each one.
In science class you learn that water, salt and sugar are different kinds of matter. Which word means 'substance'?
b1-v-ausdrucken: You need your train ticket on paper. You click a button on your computer and the page comes out of the machine.
At the office your boss asks you to put the email from your screen onto paper for the meeting.
You finish your homework on the laptop and send it to the printer so you can bring a paper copy to school. What do you do with the file?
b1-n-einfuehrung: On your first day at university, a first lecture gives a short overview of the whole course before the real lessons begin.
A new employee gets a short talk about the company and its rules before starting the real work.
The first pages of a book explain what the book is about and why the writer wrote it. Which word means 'introduction'?
b1-adj-seltsam: You hear a noise in the empty house at night, and you cannot explain where it comes from. It feels not normal at all.
Your neighbour wears a thick winter coat in the summer heat and talks to himself. His behaviour is not what people expect.
A friend suddenly stops talking to you for no reason. You say: this is really ... Which adjective means 'odd'?
b1-n-verlag: You wrote a novel and send your manuscript to the company that prints and sells books.
On the first page of a book you see the name and address of the company that brought it out.
You work in an office where editors prepare new books and magazines for sale. What kind of company is it? Which word means 'publisher'?
b1-n-geschwindigkeitsbeschraenkung: A road sign shows the number 50 in a red circle. The police may fine you if you drive faster than that.
On the motorway near the town, a sign shows 100 because of noise. It tells drivers the fastest speed they may drive.
Your driving teacher says you must always watch for signs showing the highest allowed speed. Which word means 'speed limit'?
b1-v-streiken: The train drivers refuse to work for a day because they want more pay, so no trains run.
The workers at a factory all stop working together to ask for better conditions. What are they doing?
Teachers stand outside the school with signs instead of giving lessons. Which verb means 'to strike'?
b1-adv-bisher: You are at page 100 of a 300-page book. A friend asks if it is good, and you say you have liked everything you read up to this moment.
You have lived in a new city for three months, and up to this point nothing bad has happened. Which adverb do you use?
Your teacher asks how many words you have learned until this moment. Which word means 'so far'?
b1-n-visum: You want to travel to a country that requires an official permit in your passport before you arrive. You go to the embassy to get it.
At the border the officer asks for your passport and the official permission that lets you stay in the country for 30 days.
Before a trip to the USA you check which document besides your passport you must apply for. Which word means 'visa'?
b1-adj-zentral: Your hotel is in the middle of the city, close to the main square and all the shops.
The main station is in the middle of town, so it is easy to reach from everywhere. How do you describe its position?
A teacher says the most important idea of the story is its main point. Which adjective means 'central'?
b1-n-hase: At Easter children look for chocolate figures of a long-eared animal that is said to bring colourful eggs.
In a field a wild brown animal with very long ears jumps fast away as you come close.
In an old story a very fast animal with long ears loses a race to a slow one. Which word means 'hare'?
b1-v-praesentieren: At work you stand in front of your team with slides and show the results of your project.
At university each student must show their topic to the class for ten minutes using a screen.
A company shows its new car to the press for the first time at a big event. Which verb means 'to present'?
b1-n-folie: You wrap your sandwich in a thin shiny silver sheet to keep it fresh.
In the meeting room the teacher puts a clear sheet on the overhead projector and writes on it.
The new phone has a thin plastic layer on the screen that you peel off first. Which word means 'film' or 'foil'?
b1-n-spielzeug: A toddler sits on the floor and plays with blocks, a little car and a teddy bear.
You tidy up the children's room and put the cars, dolls and puzzles back into the big box.
For your friend's daughter's birthday you look for a doll or a small train in a shop. What kind of thing is it? Which word means 'toy'?
b1-v-aufnehmen: You press the red button on your phone so that your voice and your song are saved and you can listen to them later.
A hotel has enough free rooms to take in another big group of guests tonight.
The editor decides to add your short story to the new book, so the book will now have it too. Which verb means 'to include'?
b1-n-lebenslauf: You apply for a job. Together with your letter you must send a page listing your schools, jobs and skills.
The manager reads a document that shows your education and work history in order by date.
Before an interview you prepare the one-page paper with all your past schools and jobs. Which word means 'CV'?
b1-adj-strafbar: You take a bag from a shop without paying. The police say this is an act that the law punishes.
A lawyer explains that driving without a licence is something for which you can be taken to court.
Your friend asks if copying a film illegally is allowed. You say no, you could be prosecuted. Which adjective means 'punishable'?
b1-n-umtausch: The shoes you bought are too small. You go back to the shop with the receipt and get a bigger size instead.
A sign in a shop says that within 14 days you may bring an item back and take a different one in its place.
You received a shirt as a gift in the wrong colour. At the customer service desk you swap it for another. Which word means 'exchange'?
b1-n-stempel: At the post office the clerk presses a small tool with ink onto your letter to mark the date.
At the office you press a rubber tool on a paper to mark it as received, and the company name appears in ink.
At the border an officer puts an ink mark in your passport that shows the date you entered. Which word means 'stamp'?
b1-v-verbrauchen: Your old car needs 10 litres of petrol for every 100 kilometres. It really uses a lot.
At the end of the month the family has finished all the milk and rice; nothing is left.
An old fridge takes lots of electricity every year. Which verb means 'to consume'?
b1-n-nebel: On a cold morning you cannot see the end of the street, and the cars drive slowly with their lights on.
Over the river a thick white cloud lies close to the ground, so you cannot see the other bank.
The weather report warns about low visibility on the roads because of white mist. Which word means 'fog'?
b1-adj-alternativ: The shop does not have the red bag you wanted. The seller shows you a different option you could take instead.
The main road is closed, so you look on your phone for a second route to use instead.
Your doctor says the first medicine does not work, so he suggests a different one that can take its place. Which adjective describes this other choice?
b1-n-abteilung: In a big company, you work in the group of people who handle only money matters, with its own boss.
In a hospital, you go to the section that treats only children.
In a big store, the clothes, toys and food are in separate parts on different floors. Which word means 'department'?
b1-adv-ebenso: Your colleague says 'Have a nice weekend!' and you want to wish him the same in return. Which word means 'likewise'?
Anna is tall. Her brother is exactly the same height. How do you say he is tall 'just as' much?
You need to buy bread, and you need milk too. Which word means 'as well'?
b1-v-verstecken: Before your sister's birthday you put her present in the wardrobe so she cannot find it.
In a game with children, you go behind the curtain so that the others do not see you.
A dog digs a hole in the garden and puts its bone in it so nobody finds it. Which verb means 'to hide'?
b1-n-aprikose: At the market you buy a small, soft, orange-yellow summer fruit with one stone inside, a bit like a small peach.
Your breakfast yogurt has pieces of a small, orange, velvety fruit in it.
The seller at the fruit stall holds up a small orange fruit that grows on trees in summer. Which word means 'apricot'?
b1-n-schritt: Your baby makes a first small move on his own feet and you clap.
Your doctor says you should walk ten thousand of these every day, and your phone counts them.
The teacher explains how to solve the task: first stage one, then stage two. Which word means 'step'?
b1-n-szene: In the film, the two lovers meet in the rain at the station. This short part of the film is the one you remember best.
At the theatre rehearsal the director says: let's do the part where the king enters again, from the start.
A man shouts loudly at a cashier and everyone stares at him. Your friend says he made a public fuss. Which word means 'scene'?
b1-v-erledigen: You have a list: buy stamps, pay the bill, call the doctor. At the end of the day you have done all these tasks.
Your boss asks if the report is ready, and you say you will take care of it today.
Before the holidays you go through your small jobs one by one and tick them off. Which verb means 'to take care of'?
b1-adj-noerdlich: Hamburg lies at the top of Germany on the map, far away from the Alps.
On a compass the needle points to the direction opposite south, and a cold wind comes from that side.
Sweden is in the upper part of Europe. Which adjective describes its position, 'northern'?
b1-n-dessert: After the main course the waiter asks if you want something sweet, like ice cream or cake, to finish your meal.
At home your mother cooks pasta and then brings out chocolate pudding at the end of the meal.
On a restaurant menu, after the starters and the main dishes comes the last section with sweet items. What is this section called?
b1-v-gewoehnen: You moved to a new country and at first the cold weather was hard, but after a few months it feels normal to you.
Your new shoes hurt at first, but slowly your feet become used to them.
A baby cries in his new bed at first, but after a week he accepts it as normal. Which verb means 'to get used to'?
b1-n-schildkroete: At the zoo you see a slow animal with a hard round shell on its back that pulls its head inside.
While swimming in the sea you see a big animal with a shell and flippers. Later it crawls onto the beach to lay eggs.
Your friend keeps a small pet with a shell in a glass tank and feeds it lettuce. Which word means 'turtle' or 'tortoise'?
b1-n-brust: The doctor puts a cold stethoscope on the front upper part of your body to listen to your heart.
You do push-ups and train the muscles on the front of your upper body.
At the butcher you ask for the white meat from the front part of the chicken. Which word means 'breast'?
b1-n-gefaengnis: A man who stole a lot is locked away for two years behind bars, in a building with guards.
In a film the thief escapes from the place where criminals serve their sentence.
You walk past a big building with high walls and barbed wire where convicted people live. Which word means 'prison'?
b1-adj-zukuenftig: An advert says 'Meet your ... neighbours!' about people who will move into the new building next year.
The city plans how streets should look in the year 2050, for time that has not come yet. Which adjective describes these plans?
Your friend introduces the man she will marry next month as her ... husband, because he is not yet her husband. Which adjective means 'future'?
b1-v-feststellen: At home you count your money and notice that 20 euros are missing from your wallet.
A doctor does some tests and finds out what illness you have.
The mechanic checks your car and discovers that the brakes are broken. Which verb means 'to find out'?
b1-n-wohnort: A form has a box where you must write the name of the town where you live, not your street. What is this box called?
Your bank asks you to tell them if the city where you live changes after you move.
A job advert says the employee's home town must be near the office. Which word means 'place of residence'?
b1-n-nachspeise: At a dinner invitation, the host brings out a sweet course after the main meal, and everyone says it was the best part.
In the school canteen you get a small fruit yogurt after your lunch as the sweet last course.
At your birthday party the guests finish the main food, then you serve the cake as the sweet course. Which word means that last sweet course?
b1-adv-auseinander: Two friends first sat close together; now they sit far from each other at opposite ends of the table. Which word describes the distance?
The old book is falling into separate pieces, because the pages are coming away from each other.
Two twins grow up in different cities and live far away from one another. Which adverb means 'apart'?
b1-n-buehne: At the theatre the curtain opens and the actors walk onto the raised platform in front of the audience.
At a rock concert the singer jumps up onto the raised platform where the band plays.
In your school play you wait behind the curtain before you go out in front of everyone. Which word means 'stage'?
b1-v-schaden: Smoking is not good for your lungs; it does something bad to your health.
Too much sugar can hurt your teeth over many years.
A doctor says one glass of wine will not do you any harm. Which verb means 'to harm'?
b1-adj-mild: The winter was warm and soft, so you only need a light jacket in January.
The judge gives a young man who made a small mistake a punishment that is not hard.
The doctor gives you a soap with a gentle formula that does not hurt your skin. Which adjective means 'gentle'?
b1-n-held: In a film a man saves the children from a burning house and everyone cheers for him. What is he called?
A boy dreams of becoming a brave man who saves the world, like the ones in his comic books.
In a fairy tale a young brave man fights the dragon and rescues the princess. Which word means 'hero'?
b1-n-hammer: You want to hang a picture on the wall. You need a tool to knock the nail into it.
A carpenter hits nails into wood with a heavy tool that has a metal head and a wooden handle.
In your toolbox you find pliers, a screwdriver and a heavy tool with a metal head for knocking nails. Which word names this missing tool?
b1-v-ueberraschen: You secretly plan a party for your friend and want her to be happily shocked when she opens the door.
Your husband brings you flowers for no reason. You did not expect it, and he did it to make you glad.
The test result is much better than you expected and you can hardly believe it. Which verb means 'to surprise'?
b1-n-sitz: In the cinema your ticket says row 5, place 12. What is the thing you sit on called?
The company has its main office in Frankfurt, where the managers work. What is this place called?
You buy new trousers and check the way they sit on your body, not too tight, not too loose. Which word means 'fit'?
b1-n-marmelade: For breakfast you spread a sweet fruit spread from a glass jar onto your bread.
Your grandmother cooks plums with sugar in a big pot and fills small glasses with the sweet spread.
On a shop shelf there are glasses of strawberry, cherry and orange spread to put on toast. Which word means 'jam'?
b1-adj-heimlich: Your teenage son comes home late and sneaks in quietly so that his parents do not hear him.
Two friends meet in a quiet corner and tell each other something nobody else may know.
A cat walks slowly and quietly toward a bird without being noticed. Which word means 'stealthy' or 'secret'?
b1-n-inhalt: You open a big box and look at what is inside it.
The teacher asks you to say in a few sentences what the story is about.
A list on the bottle tells you what is in it: water, sugar and lemon. Which word means 'contents'?
b1-v-absagen: It is snowing heavily, so the organisers decide the football match will not take place.
You are sick and call your friend to say you cannot come to his party after all, even though you had agreed.
The company tells the singer to stop the concert planned for Friday because of the storm. Which verb means 'to cancel'?
b1-n-diskussion: In class the students talk about school uniforms and each one gives an opinion, with arguments for and against.
At dinner your family talks for an hour about where to go on holiday, with many different opinions.
A radio programme has guests who exchange arguments about a topic. Which word means 'discussion'?
b1-n-golf-2: A tanker travels through a large bay of the sea between Iran and Saudi Arabia.
On the map of Mexico, you see the big curve of sea to the east of Texas and Florida.
A geography teacher points to a large part of the sea that cuts deep into the land. Which word means 'gulf'?
b1-v-nachdenken: Your boss asks you to join a new project. You say you need two days to think carefully before you answer.
In the exam you sit silently with your pen in your hand, thinking hard about the answer.
A friend asks whether you will move abroad. You say you will consider it. Which verb means 'to ponder'?
b1-n-terminkalender: You write down your doctor's appointment, your meeting and your friend's party in a small book that you carry around.
On your phone you have an app that lists all your meetings by day and time.
Your boss says: look in your planner, are you free on Tuesday? Which word means 'planner' or 'diary'?
b1-adj-ehrlich: You find a wallet with 100 euros and bring it to the police without taking anything. People say you tell the truth and do not steal.
Your friend asks how his new haircut looks. You say what you really think, even if it is not nice.
A cashier gives you too much change and you give it back. Which adjective describes you, 'honest'?
b1-adv-voraus: In a race you are in front of all the other runners; the others are behind you.
You go to the restaurant first to get a table, while your family comes later. You go before them.
A friend walks faster and is a few metres in front. You call 'Go on, I will follow!' Which adverb means 'ahead'?
b1-n-ernte: In autumn the farmer collects potatoes and wheat from the fields after a long summer.
After heavy rain this year, the apple trees gave few fruits. Farmers complain that what they gathered is small.
Villagers celebrate a festival to give thanks for the gathering of the crops. Which word means 'harvest'?
b1-v-wachsen: Your little son gets taller every year, and his trousers are too short again.
You plant a seed in a pot and every week the plant gets bigger.
The number of people living in the city goes up each year. Which verb means 'to grow' or 'to increase'?
b1-n-fortbildung: Your company sends you to a two-day course to learn new software skills for your job.
A teacher goes to a seminar in the holidays to learn new methods for her lessons.
A nurse takes evening classes to improve her professional skills. Which word means 'further training'?
b1-n-nichte: Your sister has a baby girl. What is the baby to you?
At the family party, your brother's six-year-old daughter gives you a drawing. Who is she to you?
Your uncle talks proudly about his brother's daughter. What is she to him? Which word means 'niece'?
b1-adj-sichtbar: On a clear day you can see the mountain from far away because nothing blocks the view.
A reflective vest makes a cyclist easy to see at night.
A message written with special ink shows nothing, until you hold it under a lamp and it appears. Which adjective means 'visible'?
b1-n-schlange: In the zoo a long thin animal without legs slides across the ground and hisses.
At the supermarket many people wait one behind the other at the till. You stand at the end of it.
On a hike your guide warns you to be careful in the grass because a long legless animal with a bite may be there. Which word means 'snake'?
b1-v-vorlesen: At bedtime your child asks you to say the words of a picture book out loud while she listens.
In class the teacher asks you to say the text in your book out loud for everybody.
Your grandfather cannot see well, so you speak the words from the newspaper aloud for him. Which verb means 'to read aloud'?
b1-n-energie: You feel tired and weak this morning, with no strength to do anything.
Your electricity bill is high, so the company that supplies power to your flat sends you a letter.
Wind and sun can produce clean power for homes. Which word means 'energy'?
